title: EdgePrime CDN spike during scheduled maintenance - uptime tally query
text:
EdgePrime CDN spike during scheduled maintenance - uptime tally query

["From: Kyle Park <kyle@edgeprime.com>
To: chloe.martin@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Cc: nisha@orbithealth.com, sre-alert@edgeprime.com
Date: Fri, 17 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: EdgePrime CDN behaviour during your maintenance window - uptime tally query

Hi Chloe and Marissa,

OrbitHealth flagged an availability blip during Redwood's scheduled maintenance on 2026-04-16. Our probes show a 7-minute elevated error rate for the OrbitHealth path between 02:14–02:21 UTC that coincide with an EdgePrime routing change. OrbitHealth is asking for the uptime accounting details since this could affect their SLA credits.

Quick summary:
- Probe fanout: 8 regional probes (we can attach logs)
- Observed 5xx spikes and timeouts from East US endpoints
- EdgePrime reports a routing cutoff at 02:12 UTC as part of their maintenance chain; they claim partial degradation not service outage

Can you confirm whether Redwood is attributing that window to (a) Redwood maintenance, (b) third-party EdgePrime, or (c) partial-degradation threshold that would not trigger credit? OrbitHealth needs a ballpark by EOD Pacific so they can decide whether to file a formal claim.

Thanks — attaching our incident report export for transparency.

—Kyle
Kyle Park
Technical Account Lead, EdgePrime
Attachments: edgeprime_incident_report_q2.pdf
", 'From: chloe.martin@redwood.ai
To: Kyle Park <kyle@edgeprime.com>, nisha@orbithealth.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, marcus.lin@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 17 Apr 2026 10:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: EdgePrime CDN behaviour during your maintenance window - uptime tally query

Thanks Kyle — appreciate the prompt context and the PDF.

Short answer: we don't have a final allocation yet. I ran a quick check on our telemetry; Redwood's maintenance window for the region was from 02:10–02:20 UTC and we have automations that mark the portion of traffic routed to a degraded path as "partial degradation" for SLO accounting. That said, the probe evidence you're sending looks like it may overlap with a third-party (EdgePrime) routing cut. We need the raw probe traces and any routing change logs from EdgePrime to reconcile across both sides.

Next steps I propose:
1) EdgePrime to provide raw probe logs (packet-level timestamps preferred) for 02:00–02:30 UTC — do you have those?
2) Redwood will pull host and routing logs + our prefix BGP change markers and return a reconciliation table with per-minute availability and whether minutes fall under Redwood maintenance or third-party effect.
3) OrbitHealth to confirm which endpoints and probe IDs they will use for formal claim (so we align on the same dataset).

Marcus — can you pull the host routing and KV-cache fallover logs for that timeframe (02:00–02:30 UTC) and share in a tarball? Priyom — please standby to run the per-minute SLA apportionment script once we have EdgePrime logs.

Chloe
Chloe Martin
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
--
Attachment note: we've requested file-level logs (probe-logs-20260417.tar.gz) — Kyle, can you confirm when you can share?', "From: Kyle Park <kyle@edgeprime.com>
To: chloe.martin@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Cc: nisha@orbithealth.com, sre-alert@edgeprime.com
Date: Sat, 18 Apr 2026 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: EdgePrime CDN behaviour during your maintenance window - uptime tally query

On Fri, Apr 17, 2026 at 10:45 AM Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Chloe: quick check — we can provide raw probe logs. Attaching a tar of probe traces (see file stub).

Hi all,

Attached are two artifacts: a raw probe tarball (probe-logs-20260417.tar.gz) and a short narrative PDF with our timeline. EdgePrime confirms we performed a prioritized routing handshake at 02:12:40 UTC to drain a border peer; that operation increased response-times for ~6 minutes as routes reconverged in a subset of POPs. We see timeouts from the OrbitHealth EastUS probe cluster at 02:14:10–02:20:15 UTC.

EdgePrime's position: this was internal to our CDN and should be considered a third-party routing transient, not Redwood-initiated maintenance — although timing overlaps your automated maintenance marker. We are open to a reconciliation matrix if Redwood wants to apportion minutes that are clearly EdgePrime-caused.

Attachment stubs: probe-logs-20260417.tar.gz, edgeprime_incident_report_q2.pdf

—Kyle
", 'From: marcus.lin@redwood.ai
To: chloe.martin@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, priyom.das@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 18 Apr 2026 15:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: EdgePrime CDN behaviour during your maintenance window - uptime tally query

Chloe / Marissa — I pulled host-level routing events and our proxy dash logs. Quick notes from an initial reconciliation:
- Redwood maintenance automation triggered at 02:10:05 UTC and placed a subset (approx 18% of orbital traffic) onto a degraded path for cache compaction.
- Key KV-cache rehydrate ops caused latency increases starting 02:10:30 UTC but error rates only exceeded our partial-degradation threshold (5% errors over 5m) at 02:13:00 UTC.
- EdgePrime's logs show their routing handshake at 02:12:40 UTC; their transient and our partial-degradation overlap from 02:13:00–02:18:30 UTC.

I attached an initial reconciliation CSV I generated (CSV stub line: minute,redwood_status,edgeprime_status,probe_errors). Given the overlap, the apportionment rules from our SLA doc recommend: assign minute-level ownership to the earliest detected party that introduced the client-impacting event. For minutes where both systems show simultaneous impact, we flag as "shared responsibility" and propose apportionment by probe-traffic fraction.

Priyom — can you run the apportion script against the attached raw probe tarball and our host logs, outputting per-minute ownership? Chloe — I'll put a short summary for OrbitHealth after we get the apportionment output.

Marcus Lin
Senior Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachments: reconciliation_summary.csv (stub)', 'From: chloe.martin@redwood.ai
To: nisha@orbithealth.com, kyle@edgeprime.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, marcus.lin@redwood.ai, priyom.das@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2026 09:00:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: EdgePrime CDN behaviour during your maintenance window - uptime tally query

Nisha — attaching the reconciled per-minute ownership table (summary inline below) and proposed next steps. Apologies for the short turnaround; we prioritized this because OrbitHealth flagged a potential credit.

Summary (per-minute buckets UTC):
- 02:10:  Redwood maintenance marker (minor latency), EdgePrime nominal — assigned to Redwood (no creditable outage)
- 02:11:  Redwood maintenance latency increases; errors < threshold — assigned to Redwood
- 02:12:  EdgePrime routing handshake begins at 02:12:40 — minute is mixed; we tag as shared responsibility
- 02:13–02:17: simultaneous probe errors; apportionment: EdgePrime 65%, Redwood 35% (see attached CSV)
- 02:18–02:20: EdgePrime-only transient (routing reconverged on Redwood endpoints) — assigned to EdgePrime

OrbitHealth — based on our SLA apportionment rules, the minutes where EdgePrime is fully or predominantly responsible are eligible for Redwood to exclude from our uptime ledger if the customer agrees those minutes fall under third-party outage exception. If OrbitHealth still wants Redwood to accept full uptime responsibility despite third-party cause, we can discuss a one-off goodwill credit, but we will need Exec approval given the precedence.

Proposed next steps:
1) OrbitHealth to confirm whether they accept the apportionment model (EdgePrime-majority minutes excluded from Redwood ledger) — reply by EOD Apr 20.
2) Kyle/EdgePrime to confirm their timeline and sign the reconciliation table so we can close this record.
3) If OrbitHealth disputes, we escalate to CS leadership for credit decision (Marissa, please advise on approvals flow).

Thanks — attaching: reconciliation_per_minute_apportionment.csv (stub), logs referenced earlier.

—Chloe
Chloe Martin
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference | Redwood-inference.com
--
[Attachment stubs: reconciliation_per_minute_apportionment.csv, probe-logs-20260417.tar.gz]
